plainTitle: Taller tower with more affordable homes approved at College Street and Henry Street

sources.label: Staff report from the Acting Director, Community Planning, Toronto and East York District

whatIsProposed.text: A 31-storey building was already approved for this site in 2024. City Council has now changed the Official Plan and zoning rules so the building can be 45 storeys instead.

citations.quote: On June 26, 2024, City Council approved an Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment application permitting a 31-storey mixed-use building
to permit a 45-storey (158.5 metres, excluding mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building

whatIsProposed.text: The number of homes goes up from 490 to 684. Of these, 545 would be affordable rental homes.

citations.quote: an increase from 490 to 684 residential dwelling units, including 545 affordable rental units

whatIsProposed.text: The 408 affordable studio units approved in 2024 stay. The change adds 137 affordable two-bedroom rental units. Both groups stay affordable for 40 years.
whatIsProposed.caveat: The two groups have different rent levels: the 408 studios are set at 100% of average market rent, and the 137 new units at the City's Affordable Rent levels.

citations.quote: The applicant proposes to retain the 408 studio units in the 2024 approval as affordable rental housing
to add 137 additional affordable two-bedroom units
secured at 100 percent of Average Market Rent (AMR) for a minimum affordability period of 40 years
with rents set at the City’s Affordable Rent levels for a 40-year affordability period

whatIsProposed.text: Retail space grows from 1,356 to 1,931 square metres. The plan has only 6 car parking spaces and 695 bicycle parking spaces.

citations.quote: An increase in overall retail space from 1,356 to 1,931 square metres
The proposal includes a total of 6 vehicular parking spaces (including 1 accessible space) at-grade.
A total of 695 bicycle parking spaces are proposed

whatIsProposed.text: The old 3-storey heritage houses on the site would be kept and built into the base of the new building.

citations.quote: including the integration of the existing three-storey semi-detached heritage buildings
are to be retained and incorporated into the proposed development

why.text: The area plan for this site allowed a height of 96 metres (31 storeys). A taller building needed a change to that plan.

citations.quote: to permit a building height of 96 metres (31 storeys), including a mechanical penthouse
The Official Plan Amendment is required to amend Site and Area Specific Policy 533 to allow the revised building height.

why.text: Staff supported the taller building. They said it fits the area, is close to Queen's Park subway station, and matches other tall buildings approved nearby.
why.caveat: This is the opinion of City staff.

citations.quote: Staff find the proposed Official Plan Amendment to SASP 533 to permit an increase in height from 31 to 45 storeys to be acceptable
the site is within 500 metres of Queens Park Station
The height is consistent with surrounding approvals

why.text: Staff say it would be one of the largest affordable housing projects in a single building in Canada.

citations.quote: making it one of the largest affordable housing development proposed in a single building in Canada

whoIsAffected.text: The site is at the southwest corner of College Street and Henry Street, in Ward 11 (University-Rosedale), across from the University of Toronto.

citations.quote: The site is located on the southwest corner of College and Henry Streets.
The University of Toronto's St. George Campus, with 3-4 storey institutional buildings along the north side of College Street.

whoIsAffected.text: Former tenants: 12 replacement rooms for rent will still be provided. Eligible former tenants can return at similar rents.

citations.quote: a total of 12 replacement rental dwelling rooms will continue to be provided in the proposed development
Eligible tenants would reserve the right to return to replacement rental housing at similar rents

whoIsAffected.text: Neighbours on nearby streets: at the community meeting, people raised concerns about ride-share and delivery traffic on Henry Street, too little parking, and the height. Council asked staff to consider requiring a traffic study, made with the community, as part of the site plan.

citations.quote: with particular concerns about the impacts of rideshare and deliveries on Henry Street
Concern that the additional height is out of scale with the surrounding area
a Transportation Impact Study, in consultation with the community, that includes a traffic mitigation and loading strategy to limit the impacts on the surrounding road network

whoIsAffected.text: The City budget: staff estimate the City and the Province give up about $54.9 million in fees, charges and property taxes for the 545 affordable units. These are not cash payments.

citations.quote: The total estimated value of financial incentives, based on 2026 rates, is $54,940,054
These incentives are not direct cash payments from the City

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The new zoning comes with a hold. The building cannot go ahead until the owner shows that sewers and water mains can handle it, or secures any needed upgrades.

citations.quote: restricting the proposed use of the lands until the conditions to lifting the holding provision, as set out in the By-law, are satisfied
have adequate capacity and supply to accommodate the development of the lands

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: City Council approved a new version of the draft zoning by-law, attached to a councillor's motion, in place of the one in the staff report. Council said the changes were minor, so no further public notice was needed.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: This page has not compared the two versions.

citations.quote: substantially in accordance with the draft Zoning By-law Amendment included as Attachment 1 to motion 1
City Council determine that these amendments are minor in nature, and pursuant to section 34(17) of the Planning Act, no further notice is required.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The traffic study is a request for staff to consider. The record does not guarantee it will be required.

citations.quote: City Council request the Executive Director, Development Review to consider securing the following as part of the site plan agreement

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The owner bought the house next door at 72 Henry Street. It is not part of this plan, but staff will check whether it has heritage value.

citations.quote: The existing detached dwelling at 72 Henry Street is not part of the application and will not be altered as a result of the proposed development.
This property will be further evaluated by staff for its heritage value
This Report recommends approval of an application to amend Official Plan Amendment 731 and Site-Specific Zoning By-law 1166-2025

committee.text: Toronto and East York Community Council held the public meeting and recommended approval. It added a request for staff to consider a traffic study.

citations.quote: The Toronto and East York Community Council held a statutory public meeting on July 8, 2026
This item was considered by Toronto and East York Community Council on July 8 and 9, 2026 and was adopted with amendments.

council.text: City Council approved the item. It swapped in a new version of the draft zoning by-law.

citations.quote: City Council adopted this item on July 29 and 30, 2026 with amendments.

whatHappensNext.text: The City's item page links this decision to By-laws 1064-2026 and 1234-2026. The detailed design still goes through site plan review, and the hold must be lifted before the building can go ahead.
whatHappensNext.caveat: The record does not give a construction date. This page has not checked whether anyone appealed.

citations.quote: See also By-laws 1064-2026
will be further addressed through the Site Plan Control process
